business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Canning of Retort River Snail Noodles (Luosifen)

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid / Bi-juridical: private law governed by the Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991, civil law tradition); public law, federal statutes, evidence, and criminal/AML matters governed by Common Law; federal-provincial shared legislative competence under the Constitution Act, 1867.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (BIT, in force 1 October 2014)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (IPPA, in force 6 September 2016)
Convention between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1986, as amended by the 2016 Protocol)
Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD/Council of Europe, in force for Canada)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), SC 2000, c 17, as amended (FINTRAC regime; Part 1 reporting, ss. 7.1 and 9.3); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part II.1 (ss. 462.31-462.5); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 13; PCMLTFA regulations amended by SOR/2021-239. Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, as amended by SQ 2023, c 7 (Bill 78 beneficial-ownership register regime requiring declaration of natural persons owning 25% or more of voting rights or equity, or exercising de facto control); Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, c P-44.1, r 3; Regulation respecting fees for legal publicity services, c P-44.1, r 5. Tax-registration integration through the Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp) and Quebec Tax Administration Act, CQLR c A-6.003.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - Quebec beneficial-ownership statements are held in a restricted register maintained by the Registraire des entreprises; accessible to the Registraire, law enforcement, FINTRAC, CRA and Revenu Quebec; not publicly searchable; home addresses of individual UBOs are kept confidential; nominee structures are not permitted to obscure the 25% threshold under federal beneficial-ownership rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association of the foreign corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / PRC notary public office of the domicile city
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PRC notarization followed by Chinese MFA/designated office apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention (effective for PRC on 7 November 2023); no Canadian consular legalization required; certified French/English sworn translation for Quebec filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate general partner issued within 30 days of the formation filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAMR enterprise credit information registry / competent PRC authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Chinese MFA; plus translation by an OTTIAQ-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authentic notarial act: limited partnership agreement (contrat de societe en commandite) executed or counter-authenticated
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in good standing, Chambre des notaires du Quebec
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Quebec notary authentic act; no apostille required for domestic execution; foreign-partner signatures authenticated by apostilled power of attorney where applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports, identity documents and tax residence evidence of all UBOs and limited partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC notary public office; embassy/consular authentication of foreign public documents where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (Chinese MFA) plus sworn French translation; PEP declaration annex signed before a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for the capital contribution (issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing licensed bank (e.g., Bank of China, Nanning/Guangxi branch or Hong Kong affiliate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified by bank seal and notary; apostilled where produced abroad; appended to the declaration of registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Quebec general partner or formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC notary public and Chinese MFA apostille office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; presented to the Registraire with the declaration and retained by counsel

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, UBOs, directors, senior officers and signatories against: OFAC SDN List; UN Consolidated List; consolidated EU/UK sanctions lists (secondary check); Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (SC 2017, c 20) registry; the domestic PEP database (Canadian federal, provincial and Quebec public-office holders); FINTRAC public advisories and FATF public statements. Foreign PEPs, including PRC state-owned enterprise officers, trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, and senior-management sign-off. Screening results must be logged and retained for a minimum of five years; suspicious transactions are reportable to FINTRAC under s. 7.1 PCMLTFA; the Revenu Quebec/PCAF anti-money-laundering cooperation regime applies.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - online portal (Registre des entreprises / RQE) at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; NUANS name search through an approved search house for federal-provincial conflicts
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), ss. 23, 63 and 67, and Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business (c C-11, r 9) require the declared legal name, firm name (enseigne) and food packaging to be in French; a non-French version may only be used subordinate to the French name, with narrow exceptions for registered trademarks and proper names. The corporate name must use the Latin alphabet; names derived from non-Latin scripts must be transliterated (pinyin for PRC-based names); Chinese ideograms in the legal name are not accepted by the Registraire. The designation for a limited partnership must read 'societe en commandite' (s.e.c.) or, if filed in English, 'limited partnership' (L.P.).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Trust / Assurance / Insurance / Pret / Loan / Valeurs / Securities - reserved to regulated financial institutions under the Bank Act and Quebec financial statutes
Universite / University and College / College - prior ministerial consent required under educational statutes
Ingenieur / Engineer and Architecte / Architect - reserved professional titles under the Professional Code, CQLR c C-26
Medecin / Doctor, Notaire / Notary, Avocat / Lawyer, Huissier / Bailiff - restricted regulated titles
Royal / Reine / Roi / Gouvernement / Municipal - Crown or public-authority connotation requiring authorization
Quebec / Montreal in the name - permitted only where the enterprise has an establishment in the geographic area and the name does not imply a public body
Canada / Federal / National - requires federal regulator consent where misleading
Corporation / Inc. / Ltd. / LLC / S.A. - prohibited where the entity is formed as a societe en commandite; only the 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.' suffix is permitted
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Rejection is communicated by written notification from the Registraire with stated grounds under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (c P-44.1). The applicant may either (i) file a new name-reservation request curing the defect, or (ii) file a written application for administrative review (demande de revision) with the Registraire within 60 days of notification, setting out legal arguments and supporting evidence; the Registraire must issue a reasoned revised decision. If the review is unfavourable, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Quebec (civil chamber) within 30 days of the review decision under the Act and the Code of Civil Procedure (CQLR c C-25.01). While the appeal is pending, counsel should file a parallel fresh reservation to protect priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited acceptance: an LP must declare a real principal establishment in Quebec with a serviceable physical address acceptable to the Registraire and Revenu Quebec. A virtual office or domiciliation service may be used only as the registered office address where the general partner maintains the actual MAPAQ-licensed production site elsewhere in Quebec; fully virtual formation without physical establishment is not permissible for a food-manufacturing LP, and the declared address must be available during business hours for process service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - quantified risk: approximately 85% probability of an unannounced MAPAQ (Ministere de l'Agriculture, des Pecheries et de l'Alimentation) hygiene and food-safety inspection of the production plant within the first 12 months of operations under the Food Products Act, CQLR c P-29; approximately 35% probability of an unannounced Revenu Quebec GST/QST or payroll verification visit during the first year; approximately 10% probability of a Registraire compliance inspection of the registered office and UBO filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991), arts. 2186-2279 on partnership generally and arts. 2236-2266 on limited partnership (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), ss. 2, 9-15, 27-28; Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) / Quebec Enterprise Registrar, Legal Publicity Branch
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite) filed through the REQ online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Partners may contribute money, property or other rights, except that a limited partner may not contribute services (CCQ art. 2243). No escrow account or capital-block deposit is required; access to capital is governed by the partnership agreement and the general partner's management authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the undersigned general partner and limited partners of the Partnership, hereby resolve as follows: 1. The Schedule of Capital Contributions is approved, and the General Partner is authorized to issue partnership interests to subscribing partners. 2. The registered office of the Partnership is fixed at 1230 Industrial Park Boulevard, Montreal, Quebec, Canada, and the General Partner is directed to file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. 3. [Name] is appointed Chief Manager to register the establishment with the CRA and Revenu Québec, open bank accounts, and retain professional advisors. 4. The actions of the General Partner to date are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and reservation of the limited partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Priorité and Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-registration name priority search against the REQ enterprise register and the Canadian trademark database. Select an exclusive proposed name including the legal element 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'/'L.P.' Submit a priorité (name reservation) request through the REQ online portal; the reservation is valid for 12 months and may be renewed.
required_dossiers: Proposed name with corporate designation (L.P./S.E.C.)
Name reservation request (REQ priorité form)
Written consent of every partner to the use of the proposed name
Certificate of trademark availability (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on distinctiveness grounds, file an amended priority request, obtain a written waiver from the owner of the conflicting name, or submit an alternative name. A refusal by the REQ may be contested within 30 days before the Court of Quebec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of the limited partnership agreement and registration dossiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel and tax advisors retained by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement in conformity with CCQ arts. 2236-2257, specifying capital contributions, profit and loss sharing, management powers of the general partner, restrictions on limited partners, and dissolution events. Concurrently draft the Declaration of Registration, identify the principal establishment in Quebec, and determine the general partner's domicile.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement
List of all general and limited partners with full identification and contribution schedules
Statement of the registered office and principal establishment in Quebec
Notarized or certified extracts of corporate partners (where applicable)
Name reservation certificate issued by the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the REQ queries a clause, amend the agreement and declaration to align with mandatory CCQ provisions, resubmit the corrected draft, and obtain counsel's conformity opinion to cure the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online filing service (Québec Enterprise Registrar Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ secure portal, complete the déclaration d'immatriculation for the limited partnership, upload partner identification, designate the general partner, provide the establishment address, and remit the filing fee. Upon acceptance, the REQ issues the enterprise registration number (NEQ) and a certificate of registration evidencing legal publicity.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration
Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
Identification documents of each individual partner and proof of existence of any corporate partner
Name reservation certificate
Receipt of the official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected for incompleteness, the REQ issues a notice of deficiency; the applicant must rectify within 30 days. A refusal of registration may be contested before the Court of Quebec within 30 days, or the applicant may file an amended declaration with full curative details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for federal and provincial tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account using Form RC1; simultaneously register with Revenu Québec for QST and source deductions using Form LM-1-V. Disclose the general partner's identity and the partnership's fiscal relationship. If the LP is interjurisdictional, complete the Canada-Quebec mandatory integrated registration election.
required_dossiers: REQ NEQ certificate and registration extract
Limited partnership agreement
Identification of the general partner and each partner resident in Canada
CRA Form RC1 and Revenu Québec Form LM-1-V
Bank-account confirmation for refund/direct-deposit linkage (where required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct and resubmit any deficient RC1 or LM-1-V. Refusals can be addressed through the CRA administrative objections process and Revenu Québec's contestation service; late registrations may attract penalties under the Excise Tax Act but can be mitigated by voluntary disclosure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal business licence and zoning clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Montreal city permit authority (Service des permis et inspections de la Ville de Montréal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal business licence application for a food-processing establishment, attach the REQ extract and lease deed, verify industrial zoning compatibility, and pay the annual licence fee. Obtain a zoning attestation confirming that the address permits a retort-food manufacturing operation.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application form
Copy of the lease or ownership certificate for the establishment
REQ registration extract and NEQ
MAPAQ permit application or confirmation of eligibility
Floor plan and description of production equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused for zoning or inspection reasons, appeal to the municipal council or the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) within 30 days, or cure the stated deficiency by modifying the premises and reapplying.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of partnership banking facilities and completion of formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I chartered bank in Canada (e.g., a major retail bank with commercial lending desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certified partnership documents, the REQ NEQ certificate, and the bank resolution of the general partner to the commercial banking officer. Execute the partnership account mandate designating authorized signatories and EFT/wire beneficiaries; complete KYC due diligence for all partners and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: REQ certificate of registration (NEQ)
Original or notarized copy of the limited partnership agreement
First Board Resolution designating the Chief Manager and signatories
Identification and proof of address of all partners
Pro-forma invoices for capital-equipment payments on swift/LC and wire rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the bank requires additional beneficial-ownership documentation, provide a REQ statement of compliance and updated declaration, or escalate to the bank's commercial adjudication team; failure to maintain REQ annual filings will trigger account hold, cured by filing the annual update and obtaining a certificate of conformity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) - Safe Food for Canadians Program; Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) - Food Products Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence (SFCA, SC 2012 c 24) for food processing, and MAPAQ Food Transformation Permit (Permis de transformateur alimentaire) under the Food Products Act (CQLR c P-29); supports retort/noodle-manufacturing trade in interprovincial and export channels

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Environmental Permits and Compliance Branch
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Authorization - Declarable activity category (Declaration of Conformity) for low-to-moderate-impact food plants under the Regulation respecting the declaration of conformity (CQLR c Q-2, r. 3.1); full prior Environmental Authorization under arts. 22 and 31.5 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) is required if the plant discharges more than 50 m3/day of process effluent or reports a high organic load.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with municipal sewer by-law and LQE art. 20 - BOD5 not exceeding 350 mg/L, TSS 500 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5, fats/oils and grease 15 mg/L; pretreatment grease traps mandatory. Air: rice-flour dust and VOC emissions must not exceed the plant's environmental authorization limits, typically PM 20 mg/m3 at the baghouse stack; odour and noise per municipal by-law. Solid waste: grease-trap sludge is agro-food residual matter subject to the Regulation respecting the recovery and valorization of residual materials (CQLR c Q-2, r. 32).
required_studies_for_full_authorization: Process treament capacity analysis (TRE characterization) for wastewater
Air dispersion modelling of flour-dust and steam emitters

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety inspection and certificate issued by the City of Montreal fire prevention bureau under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c S-3.4) and the Quebec Construction Code, Chapter I - Fire Safety; structural load certification by a licensed professional engineer covering racks, retorts, and noodle-line platforms; workplace registration and occupational-health clearance with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1) and the Regulation respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1, r. 13), including machine-guarding, lockout protocols, and food-dust hazard review.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal GST/HST (TPS/TVH) and income tax administration; online portal: CRA My Business Account / Business Registration Online. Revenu Quebec - Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), provincial income tax and employer payroll administration; online portal: Clic Revenu. Entity registration authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (NEQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) File the declaration of limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec to obtain the NEQ and registration extract; (2) register the LP with CRA via Business Registration Online or Form RC1 to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST program account (RT), payroll program account (RP), and, if imports or direct export reporting are anticipated, a customs account (RM); (3) register the LP for QST with Revenu Quebec under the same NEQ to obtain a QST registration number; (4) obtain a CBSA exporter/import program account through the CARM portal for electronic export declarations; (5) open a Canadian settlement bank account in the LP's name and satisfy FINTRAC beneficial ownership verification; (6) have the non-resident general partner and each non-resident limited partner obtain a Canadian tax identification number (CRA individual or non-resident account) for reporting Canadian-source income allocations; (7) secure the CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act licence (food export) and any provincial food-processing permit, which are prerequisites for lawful export and are referenced in the exporter's CRA/customs profile. No minimum capital is required at registration; a non-resident may hold limited partnership interests without Canadian residency restrictions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - Under the Canadian Income Tax Act (ITA) and the Quebec Taxation Act, a limited partnership is not a taxable entity; income, gains, losses, and credits flow through to partners. For GST/QST purposes, however, the LP is a separate 'person' and must register, collect, and file GST/QST as a distinct registrant. The LP carries on business in Canada and in Quebec through its general partner's management activity and manufacturing establishment, creating a Quebec permanent establishment. Tax-exempt zone status does not apply. Export-oriented manufacturers will typically be in a net GST/QST refund position due to zero-rated export supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no U.S.-style check-the-box regime; the LP is statutorily pass-through. Relevant elections include: (i) ITA s. 97(2) election to transfer property into the LP partnership on a cost/agreed-amount basis at formation; (ii) ITA s. 96(3) election for a permitted non-calendar fiscal period; (iii) ITA s. 216(1) net-basis election for a non-resident partner deriving rental income; (iv) ITA s. 152(4) waiver of the normal reassessment limitation period; (v) hybrid mismatch arrangement rules (ITA s. 18.4(2) to s. 18.6, effective 1 July 2022) which override treaty benefits and deny deductions for hybrid and branch mismatch outcomes, with designation/elective notices available in prescribed circumstances; (vi) GST/HST Quick Method election (eligibility generally limited to registrants with taxable worldwide supplies not exceeding CAD 400,000, excluding financial services); (vii) annual GST/HST filing election under ETA s. 238; and (viii) the QST Fast Method election in Quebec whereby eligible SMEs calculate net QST liability on a simplified basis. The LP's general partner must maintain the partnership books and file the prescribed partnership information returns (TP-600/RP or T5013) and allocate income to partners.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST, TPS/TVH) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST, TVQ) - a dual VAT system in which QST is computed on the GST-inclusive purchase price.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies over any four consecutive calendar quarters (identical threshold for GST/HST and QST). Mandatory registration takes effect on the first day of the month following the quarter in which the threshold is exceeded. A manufacturer exclusively exporting zero-rated goods may voluntarily register to claim input tax credits/refunds on inputs; the small-supplier exemption can be renounced by filing Form RC1 or its Quebec equivalent.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently operate a real-time tax clearance, fiscal stamping, or tax-authority API invoice approval system. CRA and Revenu Quebec accept electronic invoices provided the invoice data meet the statutory content requirements of the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act (supplier name, BN/QST registration number, date, description, quantity, taxable amount, GST/QST shown separately for transactions above the CAD 30-invoice threshold). The federal Pan-Canadian e-invoicing initiative promotes voluntary e-invoicing through the PEPPOL network (CRA pilot). Quebec has enacted a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime: enterprises with annual turnover of CAD 50 million or more must be able to receive structured e-invoices from 1 September 2026 and issue from 1 September 2027; enterprises with turnover between CAD 10 million and CAD 50 million must receive from 1 September 2027 and issue from 1 September 2028; obligations for smaller enterprises, including new SME manufacturers, are phased in under dates to be prescribed. Exporters, irrespective of size, must file electronic export declarations with the CBSA through the CARM system for goods exported with a value exceeding CAD 2,000.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of manufactured instant rice noodle products qualify for the 0% GST/HST rate under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (section 5 for goods delivered by the supplier to a carrier or consignee for export, or delivered outside Canada), provided the goods are physically exported, sold, and paid for by a non-resident in the normal course of trade. QST zero-rating applies concurrently under section 23.1 of the Regulation respecting the Quebec Sales Tax, which imports the federal zero-rating categories. Services supplied to a non-resident that relate to exported goods or constitute offshore services may also be zero-rated under Part V, section 7, provided the customer is a non-resident, not registered under the GST/QST, and the service is not performed in relation to real property situated in Canada or in respect of tangible personal property destined for a consumer in Canada. Domestic sales of instant noodles may independently qualify as zero-rated basic groceries (Schedule VI, Part III) unless the product is classified as a taxable pre-packaged snack; export zero-rating under Part V is available regardless of the domestic classification. Input tax credits and refunds are available for GST/QST paid on manufacturing inputs, giving zero-rated exporters a net-refund position; the supplier must retain supporting export evidence within the normal two-year record-keeping cycle and make the evidence available upon CRA or Revenu Quebec demand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - CBSA CARM electronic export report (formerly B13A) submitted through the Canadian Export Reporting System for goods exceeding CAD 2,000, including the exporter account identifier, H.S. classification (H.S. 1902/2008 category mapping for rice noodles), quantity, value, destination, and reason-for-export code, plus any applicable CFIA/agricultural export documentation.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill - a clean multimodal or ocean/air transport document issued by a common carrier evidencing that the goods were received in Canada and consigned to the non-resident customer at the foreign destination, showing the shipping mark, port of loading, port of discharge, INCOTERMS, and container/seal numbers.

Inward Remittance Certificate - bank evidence of settlement in Canadian dollars or convertible foreign exchange equivalent (SWIFT MT103, telegraphic transfer advice, or letter-of-credit realization statement issued by the Canadian receiving bank) evidencing payment from the non-resident buyer and completing the commercial payment audit trail within the expected settlement window.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess within the normal 4-year limitation period, extended to 10 years in cases of misrepresentation, wilful default, or fraud. Where the exporter cannot produce the export documentation bundle or where the documentation is internally inconsistent, the zero-rating will be reversed, net tax and QST will be assessed with compound daily interest at prescribed rates, and the supplier will lose entitlement to input tax credits. Civil penalties under ETA s. 280 (and the mirroring Quebec Tax Administration Act provisions) apply for false or deceptive statements and omissions: the greater of CAD 8,000 and 25% of the tax evaded or of the rebate/refund improperly claimed. Egregious misstatement penalties under ITA s. 163.2 may also be asserted against the general partner. Criminal prosecution under ETA s. 327 (fines up to 200% of evaded tax and imprisonment of up to 2 years) is available for wilful evasion or fraud in export-claim transactions. CRA and Revenu Quebec scrutinize circular exporter-customer flows, abnormally long payment terms, related-party offshore purchasers, and high-risk food-trade corridors; export proceeds received beyond the 180-day evidentiary benchmark without documented commercial credit terms will heighten audit risk and may trigger immediate suspension of refunds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); supporting regulators: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada maintains no separate foreign exchange administration or exchange control agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction with a free-floating currency and full de facto convertibility for both current account items (trade payments, dividends, interest, royalties) and capital account transactions (direct investment, loans, portfolio flows). No exchange control permits are required for inward or outward remittances. Practical profit remittance hurdles for a Quebec limited partnership are limited to Canadian non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (generally 25% on dividends, interest, rents, and royalties; reduced by tax treaties to 5-15% on dividends, 15% on interest, and often 0% on certain arm's length royalties) and the need for the partnership to file tax information returns (T5013 or NR4) and to obtain treaty-based relief (CRA Form NR301) to prevent over-withholding on distributions to non-resident partners.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement exists in Canada. Exporters are not required to convert export proceeds into Canadian dollars or to deposit them with the central bank within any timeline. Export receipt foreign currency balances may be held indefinitely in foreign currency bank accounts at Schedule I Canadian banks. For income tax and GST/HST purposes, export proceeds are translated into Canadian dollars at the Bank of Canada's noon spot rate (or the rate stipulated by the CRA) on the date of receipt; there is no mandatory conversion ratio and no FINTRAC threshold beyond the standard CAD 10,000 large cash transaction reporting requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with legal constraints. An offshore digital EMI or money services business (MSB) may operate as a limited payment/clearing conduit for a Canada-facing business only if it is registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). It must maintain a Canadian presence or agent, implement client identification, record-keeping, and suspicious transaction reporting, and cannot hold Canadian deposits. Due to the PCMLTFA and Quebec's Money-Services Businesses Act, a foreign EMI without a FINTRAC MSB registration is not a viable banking rail for the Quebec LP. Unregistered foreign EMIs should be used at most as an auxiliary collection channel, never as the primary corporate treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Schedule I Canadian banks generally require at least one authorized representative—a general partner or, if the GP is a foreign corporate entity, a designated signing officer with a valid power of attorney—to complete certified identity verification. Fully remote account opening is available at most major banks using approved digital identification services, but many institutions still require a live video interview or a physical branch visit for non-resident beneficial owners and foreign entities. For a low-risk Quebec-registered limited partnership manufacturing packaged food products, an in-branch appearance is normally waived provided the partnership is registered in the Quebec Enterprise Register (Registraire des entreprises), the general partner submits notarized ID, and the ultimate beneficial owners file certified passport and proof of address documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) opacity due to multi-tiered foreign limited partners or a corporate GP in a low-tax jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain diagram with beneficial ownership percentages; notarial certificate of the limited partnership agreement (déclaration de société en commandite); Certificate of Registration from the Registraire des entreprises; charter documents, certificate of good standing, and register of directors of the corporate general partner; current passport copies of all UBOs; notarized source-of-wealth declarations; and a legal opinion on Canadian and OECD tax-transparency standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection or a large contribution from a non-resident parent company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or reviewed financial statements of the contributing partner; bank statements evidencing the provenance of funds; executed loan agreements, promissory notes, and intercompany funding agreements; tax clearance certificates where applicable; signed senior-management declaration on the source of funds; and a transaction rationale memorandum explaining the business purpose of the capital inflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory status of the food manufacturing business — no issued Quebec food-processing licence or Safe Food for Canadians Act license at the time of onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of an application submitted to the Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ) or Safe Food for Canadians Act license; municipal zoning approval; facility inspection certificate or a timeline to meet provincial food-safety standards; detailed description and flow-chart of the instant rice noodle manufacturing process; and copies of business insurance (general liability and product liability) in force.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are remitted by SWIFT MT103 wire with a clear payment narrative identifying the sender as the investing partner, the beneficiary as the Quebec LP's bank account, and the purpose as 'Capital Contribution' or 'Paid-in Capital'. The Canadian beneficiary bank will require the underlying executed partnership agreement, the contribution schedule, a source-of-funds declaration, and, if the transfer exceeds the FINTRAC large transaction threshold, a large cash transaction report is filed through the bank. Where applicable, a SWIFT MT202/MT202COV may cover the interbank leg. To facilitate clearing, the beneficiary bank account is referenced by the Canadian bank's institution number, bank/transit number, and SWIFT BIC. An opinion letter confirming the capital contribution is not a loan and will be escorted by a statement of shareholder/partner equity may be necessary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and trade settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for open account or TT payments; for documentary trade, the preferred rail is an advised or confirmed irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by the Canadian bank and governed by UCP 600, payable by sight draft or deferred payment terms. Payments to suppliers in China, Vietnam, or other Asian markets can be made in CAD, USD, EUR, or RMB using the agreed settlement currency. Canada's payment infrastructure, including the Canadian High Value Clearing System (HVCS) and its successor Real-Time Rail (RTR), supports the domestic leg of such payments; cross-border transactions settle via SWIFT/CHIPS or correspondent banks. FINTRAC reporting thresholds apply for cash payments, and Form T1135 filing obligations apply for foreign supplier invoices and outstanding balances if the partnership holds foreign assets exceeding CAD 100,000.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/CNY, CAD/EUR)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in offshore Chinese renminbi (CNH) or restricted emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for medium- and long-term financing
European-style FX options (calls and puts) transacted with a regulated OSFI-supervised Canadian bank or broker

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Declaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the 9th month following the end of the limited partnership's fiscal year; where no fiscal year-end is adopted, no later than the 9th month following the anniversary of registration; minimum filing frequency of once every 12 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing charge accrues per day of delay and may reach CAD 200; a declaration omitted for two consecutive years authorizes the REQ to strike the LP from the register after notice, terminating the advantages of legal publicity and the opposability of the partners' limited liability to third parties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec partnership income declaration (TP-600) and partner allocation slips (Releve 15)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: TP-600 due on or before the last day of the 6th month after the end of the partnership's fiscal year; Releve 15 slips due by the end of February following the calendar year in which income is allocated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission exposes the partnership to interest, administrative penalties and fines under the Taxation Act (CQLR c. I-3), including escalating penalties for an enterprise that also fails to file a Releve 15 in accordance with the regulations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal partnership information return (T5013) with T5013 Summary and income-allocation slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the later of March 31 and the day that is five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 15 per day per slip (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 8,000) and additional penalties of CAD 25 per missing slip up to CAD 2,500; gross-negligence penalties may be levied under section 163 of the Income Tax Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec limited partnership is not subject to a general statutory audit obligation; audited financial statements become compulsory if (i) the partnership agreement or bank or lender covenants so require, (ii) the LP is a reporting issuer under the Securities Act (CQLR c. V-1.1), or (iii) Revenu Quebec or CRA specifically demands audited accounts in an audit, objection or verification context
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook: IFRS applies mandatorily to reporting issuers and to Revenu Quebec 'large enterprises' (consolidated revenue over CAD 50 million or consolidated assets over CAD 500 million); all other private limited partnerships use ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) as the default framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The statutory register of individuals with significant control under Quebec law applies to legal persons rather than partnerships; the LP must nevertheless (i) update the REQ declaration within 15 days whenever a general or limited partner is added, withdraws, transfers its interest or changes its address, (ii) confirm in each annual declaration the name, address, and capital contribution of every partner, and (iii) maintain a FINTRAC-compliant beneficial-ownership record that the LP's financial institution requires to be re-confirmed on partner changes and on an annual recertification cycle
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions, transfers, distributions and withdrawals)
Register of General Partners (names, addresses, authority and changes)
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions, Partnership Agreement and trust or contract documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 145 to USD 510 per year (CAD 200 to CAD 700) for a Quebec registered agent providing the registered establishment, mail forwarding, and statutory declaration filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,300 to USD 29,200 (CAD 10,000 to CAD 40,000) for a review or audit engagement of a mid-sized specialty food manufacturer preparing ASPE financial statements; full audits with inventory costing and multi-region revenue allocations may reach USD 40,000
